hits.snippet: G2, the Chicago-based software insights platform, agreed today to acquire three prominent software review and discovery properties from Gartner: Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp\. The deal brings four of the **largest B2B review** sites under a single roof and signals a shift toward unified, AI-driven software recommendation and buying experiences\. According to the announcement, the combined business will include roughly six million verified customer reviews and tap into an audience of more than 200 million annual software buyers\. G2 said it expects the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2026, subject to standard regulatory and closing conditions\. G2’s leadership frames the agreement as a response to fragmentation in the software buying journey\. By consolidating multiple review databases and audiences, the company aims to streamline discovery for buyers and expand demand-generation tools for vendors\. In a public post, G2’s CEO described the integration as building “the trusted data foundation for B2B software in the age of AI,” with deeper buyer intent signals and a more consistent taxonomy across categories\. Stamford-based Gartner acquired Capterra, an Arlington, Va\.-based company that posts reviews of business software penned by the people who use the applications\. Capterra allows users to rate software applications and share details on the pros and cons of using them\. Between the 2007 launch of its software feedback service and this past July, Capterra users have posted 25,000 software reviews on the company’s website\. Gartner \(NYSE: IT\) did not immediately state what it paid for Capterra, whose CEO Michael Ortner credited its success in part to a failed attempt to raise venture capital in 2007\. “I am absolutely convinced that if we had succeeded in raising money when we first started out that we would no longer be around today,” Ortner stated in a November 2014 blog\. “Some businesses just take time—time to think it through, time for the market to catch up, time to play with the product long enough to get it just right\. # Why isn’t my brand showing up when AI chatbots recommend products? Similarweb AI Search Intelligence tracks brand mentions, citation gaps, share of voice, sentiment, and traffic across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Google AI Mode\. A brand is often missing because AI chatbots can recognize it but do not see enough third-party proof, entity clarity, or source coverage to trust it in a recommendation set\. ## Why isn’t my brand showing up when AI chatbots recommend products in my category? AI systems do not reward recognition alone; they reward a short list they can defend\. A model can know a brand exists, yet still leave it out when the prompt requires a recommendation set, such as “best ecommerce PPC agency UK” or “best CRM for mid-market SaaS\.” That usually means your site is not the only missing asset; your source pool is\. If the brand shows up on your homepage but not in G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, industry publications, or comparison pages, the model has too little outside validation to quote you with confidence\. In B2B and SaaS, that gap matters more than old-school ranking alone\. ## How do you audit the gap with Similarweb AI Search Intelligence?
